# OpenClaw 🦞 — 您的助手，在您的设备上，在您的聊天中

OpenClaw是一款开源人工智能助手，可在您的个人电脑上运行，并在您已使用的渠道中与您互动：Discord、iMessage、Slack、Teams、Telegram、WhatsApp以及20多个其他渠道，还有适用于macOS、iOS、Android、Windows和Linux的本地应用程序。One Gateway 在笔记本电脑上将其作为个人助手运行，或者 作为共享的[多人抓娃娃机](https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/multiplayer)；配置是唯一的区别。 **属于您，没有陷阱。**状态、内存和凭据都驻留在您的硬件上。模型和代理框架（Claude、Codex、本地模型）是插件，您可以进行替换，而无需更改其他任何内容。您的提示将发送给您配置的模型提供商和聊天平台，以及您启用的任何诊断导出功能。 自己启用；默认情况下，OpenClaw 本身只会回传每日版本检查信息，匿名功能统计数据为选择性启用，而 `update.checkOnStart: false` 会禁用这两项功能（[OpenClaw 会回传哪些信息](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/telemetry))。OpenClaw 由[OpenClaw 基金会]管理 (https://openclaw.org)，一个独立的501(c)(3)组织，不设付费等级、托管服务或代币。架构案例（可信网关、不可信执行、通过代码强制执行的策略）请参阅[为什么选择OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/why-openclaw)。 [网站](https://openclaw.ai) · [文档](https://docs.openclaw.ai) · [入门指南](https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started) · [为什么选择 OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/why-openclaw) · [常见问题](https://docs.openclaw.ai/help/faq) · [愿景](VISION.md) · [DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/openc law/openclaw) 安装 安装程序支持 macOS、Linux 和 Windows。它会在需要时提供受支持的 Node.js 运行时。 ```bash # macOS / Linux / WSL2 curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash ``` ```powershell # Windows PowerShell iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` 已经在管理 Node.js 了吗？改为安装已发布的软件包（24.x 上的 Node 24.16.0+ 或 26.1.0+；出于安全考虑，强烈建议使用 24.22.1+/26.12.1+）： ```bash npm install -g openclaw@latest --allow-scripts=openclaw ``` 该命令适用于 npm 12 或 npm 11.16+。在 npm 11.15 及更早版本中，请省略 `--allow-scripts=openclaw`。请参阅 有关生命周期脚本合约、Docker、Nix 和其他部署路径的 合约、Docker、Nix 和其他部署路径。 快速启动 在新安装时，安装程序脚本会自动开始引导流程。 完成它们打开的向导。如果您直接使用 npm、 pnpm 或 Bun 安装的，请运行： ```bash openclaw onboard --install-daemon ``` 入驻后： ```bash openclaw gateway status openclaw dashboard ``` 引导流程会验证模型访问权限、创建工作区并配置网关。最后一条命令将打开控制界面；请在该界面发送一条消息，以确认助手是否正常工作。请参阅[入门指南](https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started)，了解频道设置和故障排除。 ## 如何将它们结合起来 - [网关](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway)是会话、工具、事件和频道连接的本地控制平面。 - [控制UI](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui)、CLI和[TUI](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/tui)连接到网关。 - [通道](https://docs.openclaw。 ai/channels) 将助手引入 WhatsApp、Telegram、Slack、Discord、Google Chat、Signal、iMessage 和其他消息服务。 - [配套应用程序和节点](https://docs.openclaw.ai/platforms)在受支持的平台上添加语音、Canvas、摄像头、屏幕和设备本地操作。 OpenClaw与托管和本地[模型提供商](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers)合作。其[工具](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools)、[技能](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skills)和[插件](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins)扩展了助手的能力。 安全 将入站消息视为不受信任的输入。支持私信的频道默认与未知发件人配对；使用“openclaw pairing approve ”批准配对请求。 除非您配置了沙盒，否则工具将在主机上运行，用于主会话。请先阅读[安全指南](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security)、[漏洞披露操作手册](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security/exposure-runbook)和[沙盒指南](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/sandboxing)

“996”工作制是指一种非正式的工作安排（上午 9 点至晚上 9 点，每周 6 天），这种工作安排正变得越来越普遍。为鼓励“996”工作制的公司工作通常意味着每周至少工作 60 小时。

g/wiki/996_working_hour_system )，了解更多详情。

# 受卡帕西启发的Claude代码指南

> 看看我的新项目[Multica](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica)——一个用于运行和管理具有可重用技能的编码代理的开源平台。
>

一个名为`CLAUDE.md`的单个文件，用于改进Claude Code的行为，该文件源自[Andrej Karpathy对LLM编码陷阱的观察](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2015883857489522876)。

英语 | [简体中文](./README.zh.md)

## 问题

摘自Andrej的帖子：

> “模型会替您做出错误的假设，然后就照着这些假设运行，而不进行核查。它们不会处理自己的困惑，不会寻求澄清，不会指出不一致之处，不会提出权衡，也不会在应该提出异议时提出异议。”

> “他们真的很喜欢把代码和API搞得过于复杂，让抽象变得臃肿，不清理死代码……在100行代码就能搞定的情况下，却要实现一个超过1000行的臃肿结构。”

> “他们有时仍然会更改/删除他们不完全理解的注释和代码，即使这些注释和代码与任务正交，也会将其视为副作用。”

解决方案

一份文件中包含直接解决这些问题的四项原则：

| Principle | Addresses |
|-----------|-----------|
| **Think Before Coding** | Wrong assumptions, hidden confusion, missing tradeoffs |
| **Simplicity First** | Overcomplication, bloated abstractions |
| **Surgical Changes** | Orthogonal edits, touching code you shouldn't |
| **Goal-Driven Execution** | Leverage through tests-first, verifiable success criteria |

## 四项原则的详细说明

### 1. 编码前先思考

**不要妄下结论。不要掩饰困惑。坦诚说明权衡取舍。**

LLM通常会默默地选择一种解释，并以此为准。这一原则迫使模型进行显式推理：

- **明确说明假设** — 如果不确定，要提问而不是猜测
- **提出多种解释** — 存在歧义时，不要默默地做出选择
- **有必要时提出异议** — 如果有更简单的方法，请说出来
- **感到困惑时停下来** — 指出不清楚的地方，并要求澄清

### 2. 简洁至上

**解决问题的最少代码。不包含任何猜测。**

抵制过度设计的倾向：

- 没有超出要求的功能
- 不对一次性代码进行抽象
- 没有未被要求的“灵活性”或“可配置性”
- 不对不可能的情况进行错误处理
- 如果200行代码可以缩减为50行，请重写

**测试：**资深工程师是否会认为这过于复杂？如果是，请简化。

### 3. 手术变化

**只触摸必须触摸的东西。只清理您自己弄脏的地方。**

编辑现有代码时：

- 不要“改进”相邻的代码、注释或格式
- 不要重构没有问题的代码
- 遵循现有风格，即使您会以不同的方式处理
- 如果您注意到无关的死代码，请指出，不要删除

当您的更改导致出现孤立项时：

- 删除因您的更改而不再使用的导入/变量/函数
- 除非被要求，否则不要删除已存在的死代码

**测试：**每行更改都应直接追溯到用户的请求。

### 4. 以目标为导向的执行

Open Source Society University

Path to a free self-taught education in Computer Science!

目 录 - [Summary](#summary) - [Community](#community) - [Curriculum](#curriculum) - [Code of conduct](#code-of-conduct) - [Team](#team) 总结 The OSSU curriculum is a **complete education in computer science** using online materials. It's not merely for career training or professional development. It's for those who want a proper, *well-rounded* grounding in concepts fundamental to all computing disciplines, and for those who have the dis cipline, will, and (most importantly!) good habits to obtain this education largely on their own, but with support from a worldwide community of fellow learners. It is designed according to the degree requirements of undergraduate computer science majors, minus general education (non-CS) requirements, as it is assumed most of the people following this curriculum are already educated outside the field of CS. The courses themselves are among the very best in t he world, often coming from Harvard, Princeton, MIT, etc., but specifically chosen to meet the following criteria. **Courses must**: - Be open for enrollment - Run regularly (ideally in self-paced format, otherwise running multiple times per year) - Be of generally high quality in teaching materials and pedagogical principles - Match the curricular standards of the [CS 2013](CURRICULAR_GUIDELINES.md): Curriculum Guidelines for Undergraduate Degree Programs in Computer Science When no course meets the above criteria, the coursework is supplemented with a book. When there are courses or books that don't fit into the curriculum but are otherwise of high quality, they belong in [extras/courses](extras/courses.md) or [extras/readings](extras/readings.md). **Organization**. The curriculum is designed as follows: - *Intro CS*: for students to try out CS and see if it's right for them - *Core CS*: corresponds roughly to the first three years of a computer science curriculum, taking classes that all majors would be required to take - *Advanced CS*: corre sponds roughly to the final year of a computer science curriculum, taking electives according to the student's interests - *Final Project*: a project for students to validate, consolidate, and display their knowledge, to be evaluated by their peers worldwide **Duration**. It is possible to finish within about 2 years if you plan carefully and devote roughly 20 hours/week to your studies. Learners can use [this spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1y2kMsIg9VaHMVmw35x_aH1hpty3V-ZMuV2jA13P_Cgo/copy) to estimate their end date. Make a copy an d input your start date and expected hours per week in the `Timeline` sheet. As you work through courses you can enter your actual course completion dates in the `Curriculum Data` sheet and get updated completion estimates. > **Warning:** While the spreadsheet is a useful tool to estimate the time you need to complete this curriculum, it may not always be up-to-date with the curriculum. Use the [OSSU CS website](https://cs.ossu.dev) or [the repo](https://github.com/ossu/computer-science) to see what courses to do. **Cost**. All or nearly all course material is available for free. However, some courses may charge money for assignments/tests/projects to be graded. Note that both [Coursera](https://www.coursera.support/s/article/209819033-Apply-for-Financial-Aid-or-a-Scholarship?language=en_US) and [edX](https:/ /courses.edx.org/financial-assistance/) offer financial aid. Decide how much or how little to spend based on your own time and budget; just remember that you can't purchase success! **Process**. Students can work through the curriculum alone or in groups, in order or out of order. - We recommend doing all courses in Core CS, only skipping a course when you are certain that you've already learned the material previously. - For simplicity, we recommend working through courses (es pecially Core CS) in order from top to bottom. Some students choose to study multiple courses at a time in order to vary the material they are working on in a day/week. A popular option is to take the math courses in parallel with the introductory courses. Course prerequisites are listed to help you determine if you are prepared for a given course. - Courses in Advanced CS are electives. Choose one subject (e.g. Advanced programming) you want to become an expert in and take all the courses under that heading. You can also create your own custom subject; the Discord community may provide feedba ck on your planned subject. **Content policy**. If you plan on showing off some of your coursework publicly, you must share only files that you are allowed to. *Respect the code of conduct* that you signed in the beginning of each course! **[How to contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)** **[Getting help](HELP.md)** (Details about our FAQ and chatroom) 社区 - We have a Discord server! [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/744385009028431943.svg?label=&logo=discord&logoColor=ffffff&color=7389D8&labelColor=6A7EC2)](https://discord.gg/wuytwK5s9h) This should be your first stop to talk with other OSSU students. Why don't you introduce yourself right n ow? [Join the OSSU Discord](https://discord.gg/wuytwK5s9h) - You can also interact through GitHub issues. If there is a problem with a course, or a change needs to be made to the curriculum, this is the place to start the conversation. Read more [here](CONTRIBUTING.md). - Add **Open Source Society U niversity** to your [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/school/11272443/) profile!
